weeks.theme: Convolutional neural networks from first principles
weeks.goal: Compute convolution, pooling and receptive fields by hand, build a small CNN, and read what it looks at.

lessons.title: Convolution by hand
lessons.build: Problem 6.1.1: convolve the 5 x 5 image with the right-minus-left kernel. Problem 6.1.2: output sizes of two real layers (Practice 1: n = 28, k = 5, p = 0, s = 1 gives 24). Problem 6.1.3: parameters of a conv layer versus a dense layer on a 224 x 224 colour image.
lessons.ask: Why does weight sharing make a conv layer need so many fewer parameters than a dense layer?
lessons.learn: Read 6.1: convolution by hand, kernels, padding, stride, output size, parameter counts.

lessons.title: Pooling, receptive field, a CNN in NumPy
lessons.build: Problem 6.2.1: max-pool a 4 x 4 grid holding 0 to 15. Problem 6.2.2: receptive field of the stack (Practice 6: three 3 x 3 convs give 7). Problem 6.2.3: gradient-check the conv layer, train the CNN and compare with a dense network. Problem 6.2.4: the position test.
lessons.ask: Why does a CNN trained on lines in the left half still find lines in the right half?
lessons.learn: Read 6.2: pooling, receptive field, translation, a CNN in NumPy.

lessons.title: Architectures from LeNet to ConvNeXt
lessons.build: Problem 6.3.1: count LeNet-5's parameters. Problem 6.3.2: gradient at the input of a 50-layer ReLU network with and without skip connections. Problem 6.3.3: bottleneck block parameters on 256 channels. Problem 6.3.4: parameters for 128 to 256 channels with a 3 x 3 kernel (294,912 weights).
lessons.ask: Why do skip connections let a 50-layer network train when a plain one will not?
lessons.learn: Read 6.3: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet and bottlenecks, ConvNeXt.

lessons.title: 1D and 3D convolutions, and when to use a CNN
lessons.build: Problem 6.4.1: output sizes for a 1D and a 3D layer. Problem 6.4.2: describe a tiny 1D CNN that finds a spike in 1,000 hourly delivery times: kernel size, channels, pooling, output. Write when a CNN is the wrong tool.
lessons.ask: Which property of the data makes a convolution the right bias?
lessons.learn: Read 6.4: 1D and 3D convolutions, sequences, volumes, and the rules for choosing a CNN.

weeks.theme: Transfer learning and fine-tuning for images
weeks.goal: Fine-tune a pretrained image model safely: choose what to freeze, set layer-wise learning rates, and augment data without leaking.

lessons.title: Why transfer learning works
lessons.build: Problem 7.1.1: count how much a head swap trains in ResNet-18 (11,689,512 parameters). Practice 1 check: Linear(1024, 20) has 1024 x 20 + 20 = 20,500 parameters. Write which layers hold general edges and which hold task-specific features.
lessons.ask: Why do early layers transfer to a new task better than late layers?
lessons.learn: Read 7.1: why transfer learning works, features at each depth, when it fails.

lessons.title: The fine-tuning recipe
lessons.build: Problem 7.2.1: discriminative learning rates for 5 groups. Problem 7.2.2: Adam at 1e-3 on every layer drops accuracy from 82%; write the fix (freeze first, lower rates, keep normalisation sane). Practice 4 check: only Linear(2048, 4) trainable gives 8,196 parameters.
lessons.ask: Why can a large learning rate on a pretrained backbone destroy what it already knows?
lessons.learn: Read 7.2: freezing, learning rates, normalisation layers, the two-stage recipe.

lessons.title: Augmentation and dataset care

lessons.learn: Read 7.3: augmentation, mixup, dataset checks, leakage between train and validation.
